weapons.name: Unarmed Attack
weapons.description: Punches and kicks add the attacker's Punch skill level to the damage done. Unarmed damage is always non-lethal unless the attacker chooses otherwise.

weapons.name: Knife
weapons.description: A common blade, easily hidden and just as easily thrown at close range.

weapons.name: Club
weapons.description: A length of wood, pipe, or scavenged debris pressed into service as a bludgeon. Damage is always non-lethal unless the wielder wants otherwise, and it costs nothing to scrounge one up.

weapons.name: Spear
weapons.description: A simple thrusting weapon, cheap to make and easy enough to hurl in a pinch.

weapons.name: Sword
weapons.description: Not every collapsed nation has convenient racks of firearms lying around; a well-kept blade is reliable when the ammo runs out.

weapons.name: Axe
weapons.description: A hand axe, equally useful for chopping wood or hostile mutants.

weapons.name: Big Sword
weapons.description: A massive two-handed blade. Its bulk makes it impossible to ready anything in the off-hand.

weapons.name: Big Club
weapons.description: A great two-handed bludgeon, from sledgehammer to fence post. Damage is always non-lethal unless the wielder wants otherwise.

weapons.name: Big Axe
weapons.description: A heavy, two-handed felling axe repurposed for combat.

weapons.name: TL4 Knife
weapons.description: A high-tech knife with a monomolecular edge or integral thermal cutting surface, capable of harming targets in full-suit powered armor.

weapons.name: TL4 Sword
weapons.description: A high-tech blade with vibrating serrations or a thermal edge, capable of harming targets in full-suit powered armor.

weapons.name: TL4 Big Sword
weapons.description: A two-handed high-tech blade with a monomolecular edge, capable of harming targets in full-suit powered armor.

weapons.name: TL4 Club
weapons.description: A high-tech baton, its impact surface augmented to shatter targets even through the best modern plating. Damage is always non-lethal unless the wielder wants otherwise.

weapons.name: Light Pistol
weapons.description: A small, easily concealed sidearm favored for its light recoil.

weapons.name: Heavy Pistol
weapons.description: A large-caliber handgun favored for its tissue-wrecking efficiency over precision.

weapons.name: Primitive Bow
weapons.description: A wood, sinew, and horn bow favored by wastelander tribals with no access to more sophisticated materials. Reloads with a Move action, or an On Turn action for a user with at least Shoot-1.

weapons.name: Modern Bow
weapons.description: A modern compound or recurve bow with sights and cams that make it considerably easier to use effectively than a primitive bow. Reloads with a Move action, or an On Turn action for a user with at least Shoot-1.

weapons.name: Rifle
weapons.description: A bolt-action or lever-action hunting rifle, the mainstay of survivors who can find one.

weapons.name: Combat Rifle
weapons.description: A selective-fire military rifle. May burst fire, expending three rounds for +2 to hit and damage.

weapons.name: Submachine Gun
weapons.description: A compact, selective-fire carbine favored for close quarters. May burst fire, expending three rounds for +2 to hit and damage.

weapons.name: Shotgun
weapons.description: A venerable double-barrel or pump shotgun. Slug ammunition doubles its normal and maximum ranges but reduces damage by 1.

weapons.name: Semi-Auto Shotgun
weapons.description: A tubular-magazine semi-automatic shotgun. Slug ammunition doubles its normal and maximum ranges but reduces damage by 1.

weapons.name: Combat Shotgun
weapons.description: A modern select-fire combat shotgun. May burst fire, expending three rounds for +2 to hit and damage. Slug ammunition doubles its normal and maximum ranges but reduces damage by 1.

weapons.name: Sniper Rifle
weapons.description: A heavy bolt-action rifle with the reach to pick off targets at extreme range. If not fired from a solid rest it performs no better than a regular rifle.

weapons.name: Automatic Rifle
weapons.description: A barely man-portable weapon meant to hurl vast amounts of lead. Each magazine costs ten times as much ammunition as a conventional round, where it can be bought at all. Can fire to suppress if braced or prone.

weapons.name: Grenade, Flash
weapons.description: Grenades always attack against AC 10; on a miss they land 1d10 meters off in a random direction. Victims within 5 meters without eye and ear protection make a Physical save or lose their next Main Action and take -2 to AC and hit rolls for 1d6 rounds.

weapons.name: Grenade, Frag
weapons.description: Grenades always attack against AC 10; on a miss they land 1d10 meters off in a random direction. Inflicts damage on all within 5 meters, Evasion for half, reduced by 1 per point of AC above 14.

weapons.name: Grenade, Gas
weapons.description: Grenades always attack against AC 10; on a miss they land 1d10 meters off in a random direction. Creates a 5-meter cloud of choking gas that disperses in one round, non-lethal damage halved on a Physical save, useless against breathing protection, and provides full concealment.

weapons.name: Grenade, Smoke
weapons.description: Grenades always attack against AC 10; on a miss they land 1d10 meters off in a random direction. Creates the same dome of opaque, harmless smoke as a gas grenade; IR or augmented visuals see through it.

weapons.name: Laser Pistol
weapons.description: A standard-issue frontier sidearm, cheap and simple to build. Not normally available for sale. Gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil, but suffers -4 to hit shooting into heavy smoke or particulates.

weapons.name: Laser Rifle
weapons.description: The standard rifle of most frontier-world armed forces. Not normally available for sale. Gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil, but suffers -4 to hit shooting into heavy smoke or particulates.

weapons.name: Shear Rifle
weapons.description: An elegantly silent weapon requiring sophisticated gravitic tech, cleaving targets into neatly sliced pieces. Not normally available for sale. Gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil, but suffers -4 to hit shooting into heavy smoke or particulates.

weapons.name: Blackout Rifle
weapons.description: A non-lethal Harmony Bureau weapon that hits targets with a phased electrical charge, dropping them unconscious. Victims reduced to zero hit points wake up ten minutes later with 1 HP. Not normally available for sale. Gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil.

weapons.name: Cutter Rifle
weapons.description: A simpler, much louder insurgent-built weapon than the shear rifle it emulates. Not normally available for sale. Gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil, but suffers -4 to hit shooting into heavy smoke or particulates.

weapons.name: Heavy Cutter
weapons.description: A great bulky cutter rifle tuned for suppressive fire. Not normally available for sale. Can fire to suppress if braced or prone; gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil, but suffers -4 to hit shooting into heavy smoke or particulates.

weapons.name: Mag Pistol
weapons.description: A hunter's sidearm that accelerates its bolts through a pulse of staged magnetics. Not normally available for sale.

weapons.name: Mag Rifle
weapons.description: A big-game hunter's staged-magnetic rifle, popular for its lack of dependence on chemical propellant. Not normally available for sale.

weapons.name: Thermal Pistol
weapons.description: Discharges a sphere of coherent plasma that causes large-scale tissue destruction, though the wounds tend to self-cauterize. Not normally available for sale. Gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil.

weapons.name: Plasma Projector
weapons.description: A heavier plasma weapon than the thermal pistol, for less cooperative targets. Creatures resistant to heat resist its damage. Not normally available for sale. Gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil.

weapons.name: Whip Beam
weapons.description: A specialist breaching tool whose pencil-thin plasma beam can cut a man-sized hole in a steel door or similar barrier as a Main Action. Not normally available for sale. Gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil.

weapons.name: Spike Thrower
weapons.description: Augments traditional shotgun mechanics with microforged, mag-accelerated flechettes, inflicting horrific damage at short reach. Not normally available for sale.

weapons.name: Neutron Blaster
weapons.description: Projects heavy particles that do no damage to unliving objects but tear apart living flesh in a one-meter-wide line out to thirty meters, requiring separate hit and Traumatic Hit rolls against each target in the line. Not normally available for sale. Gains a +1 bonus to hit from a lack of recoil.

weapons.name: Anti-Materiel Rifle
weapons.description: A bulky rifle capable of shooting out a car's engine block. If not fired from a stationary rest or prone, treat as a regular rifle. Its Trauma Die can inflict Traumatic Hits on drones, vehicles, and other machines.

weapons.name: Grenade Launcher
weapons.description: Usually an under-barrel accessory to a conventional rifle, adding 1 Encumbrance to its bulk. Fires special grenades with normal grenade effects and an AC 10 hit roll out to its own range; the modded rifle can fire either the launcher or the rifle itself on a given round, not both.

weapons.name: Demo Charge
weapons.description: Must be hand-placed but can be remotely triggered. Anything within a cone out to its maximum range takes damage, Evasion for half. Applied carefully to a vehicle or door, the object is destroyed. Its Trauma Die can inflict Traumatic Hits on drones, vehicles, and other machines.

weapons.name: Heavy Machine Gun
weapons.description: So bulky as to require a fixed position or prepared rest. Each magazine costs twenty times the ammunition of an ordinary round, but given time it can saw through reinforced concrete. Can fire to suppress if fixed to a stationary firing position. Its Trauma Die can inflict Traumatic Hits on drones, vehicles, and other machines.

weapons.name: Mortar
weapons.description: Lobs indirect fire with a minimum range of 20 meters. Always targets AC 20 at first, gaining +1 per round of continued fire on the same target if a forward spotter adjusts the aim. Acts as a frag grenade on the target point but does 3d6 base damage in a 10-meter radius; armor does not lessen the harm.

weapons.name: Rocket Launcher
weapons.description: A single-shot disposable launcher, suffering -4 to hit human-sized targets directly, though a miss still does frag grenade damage to anything within 5 meters. Anti-armor warheads lose the miss damage but do double damage to vehicles or obstacles. Its Trauma Die can inflict Traumatic Hits on drones, vehicles, and other machines.

weapons.name: Land Mine, Anti-Personnel
weapons.description: Activates on any human-sized approach within 1 meter, inflicting damage in a 2-meter radius with an Evasion save for half.

weapons.name: Land Mine, Anti-Vehicle
weapons.description: Only activated by vehicular levels of ground pressure or vehicle-sized proximate metal masses, doing its damage in a 5-meter radius. Humans caught in the blast get an Evasion save for half damage. Its Trauma Die can inflict Traumatic Hits on drones, vehicles, and other machines.

weapons.name: Railgun
weapons.description: Upscaled fixed-emplacement mag weaponry favored for defending Terran Mandate military positions. Not man-portable; typically mounted on a vehicle or fortification. Can fire to suppress if fixed to a vehicle or stationary firing position. Its Trauma Die can inflict Traumatic Hits on drones, vehicles, and other machines.

weapons.name: Anti-Vehicle Laser
weapons.description: A large fixed laser modulated to do exceptional damage to armor plate. Against vehicles or hard targets, damage is rolled twice and the better result used; against vehicles, its Trauma Die becomes a d20. Not man-portable; typically mounted on a vehicle or fortification.

weapons.name: Hydra Array
weapons.description: Spams missiles: three hit rolls divided among up to three targets. Hit and damage rolls are made normally, but a single target only takes the heaviest hit of any missiles that connect. Not man-portable; typically mounted on a vehicle or fortification.

weapons.name: Wheatcutter Belt
weapons.description: Found largely on Mandate riot control vehicles and defensive fixtures. When detonated, all creatures within 10 meters of that side of the vehicle make an Evasion save for half shrapnel damage; those within 20 meters take half damage and can save to take none. Not man-portable; typically mounted on a vehicle or fortification.

armor.name: Normal Clothing/Unarmored
armor.description: Ordinary street clothes with no protective value. Subtle.

armor.name: Leathers or Animal Hides
armor.description: Heavy leather jackets, boiled leather plates, or thick furs. Subtle. Primitive: gives no benefit against gunfire, explosives, or TL4+ melee weapons.

armor.name: Protective Sport Gear
armor.description: Dirt bike gear, athletic pads, and other sporting protection pressed into service. Obvious. Primitive: gives no benefit against gunfire, explosives, or TL4+ melee weapons.

armor.name: Scrap Mail
armor.description: Jury-rigged mail fashioned from small pieces of scavenged metal, still ineffective against bullets. Obvious, Heavy (-1 to Sneak or Exert checks). Primitive: gives no benefit against gunfire, explosives, or TL4+ melee weapons.

armor.name: Plate Carrier
armor.description: Modern ballistic plate carrier, some of the best gear a modern-day scavenger can generally hope to get. Obvious.

armor.name: Military Body Armor
armor.description: Full military-grade body armor, one of the best protective options a modern-day scavenger can generally hope to get. Obvious, Heavy (-1 to Sneak or Exert checks).

armor.name: Scrap Plate
armor.description: Jury-rigged plate armor pieced together from scavenged sheet metal. Still ineffective against bullets, but enough battered plating makes a wearer very difficult to harm with less sophisticated tools. Obvious, Heavy (-1 to Sneak or Exert checks). Primitive: gives no benefit against gunfire, explosives, or TL4+ melee weapons.

armor.name: High-Tech Street Clothing
armor.description: Ancient pre-collapse street couture fabricated from exotic materials capable of resisting blades and punctures. Its style may be outlandish, but its durability makes it valuable to scavengers. Subtle.

armor.name: Terran Explorer Suit
armor.description: A rustic outfit fashioned in the latter years of the Mandate for bold citizens roaming the uninhabited wilds of Old Terra. Built-in suit tech keeps the wearer clean and dry, identifies toxic foodstuffs on touch, and keeps them warm in anything short of a blizzard. Subtle.

armor.name: Insurgent Armor
armor.description: A catch-all for the homemade suits of armor pieced together by rebels, malcontents, and other enemies of the Harmony Bureau. Inelegant, but the makeshift tech and repurposed materials of Old Terra make for extremely sturdy protective gear. Obvious.

armor.name: Harmony Armor
armor.description: The sinister glossy-black plate worn by enforcers of the Mandate's Bureau of Harmony. Its ultra-light materials shift slightly to obscure the wearer's body shape, and its blank faceplate and voice distortion module conceal their identity. Obvious.

armor.name: Vacc Suit
armor.description: Provides a sealed, heated environment for up to six hours on a tank of air, requiring one Type A power cell for every twelve hours of use. Lowers radiation exposure, decreasing Radiation save intervals by one step. Obvious. Sealed-suit armor, unusable by wearers without a basically human body plan.

armor.name: Assault Suit
armor.description: The most common form of powered armor surviving after the collapse of the Mandate. Voraciously power-hungry, requiring a Type B power cell for 24 hours of operation, but provides encrypted military comms, vacc suit functionality, low-light and infrared visuals, and an energy feed port. Renders the wearer immune to harm from unarmed attacks, grenades, or weapons of TL3 or lower. Obvious. Sealed-suit armor, unusable by wearers without a basically human body plan. Not normally available for sale.

armor.name: Protection Field
armor.description: A rare, exotic defensive screen once used by high-ranking Mandate officials, its physical component nothing more than a ring, bracelet, or other token. Shields the wearer with an invisible force field with vacc suit functionality, imperceptible except for a brief flash when struck. Operates indefinitely on its own internal power source. Renders the wearer immune to harm from unarmed attacks, grenades, or weapons of TL3 or lower. Subtle. Not normally available for sale.

armor.name: Vanguard Plate
armor.description: Once reserved for the personal guard of high-level Mandate functionaries. Has all the functionality of an assault suit, increases the wearer's effective Strength to 18, and grants a bonus Main Action in the first round of combat. Requires the same Type B energy cell as an assault suit. Renders the wearer immune to harm from unarmed attacks, grenades, or weapons of TL3 or lower. Obvious. Sealed-suit armor, unusable by wearers without a basically human body plan. Not normally available for sale.

armor.name: Shield
armor.description: Grants a base AC of 14, or +1 to AC if it is already equal or higher, and prevents the first instance of Shock a user suffers each round. Obvious. Primitive: gives no benefit against bullets or high-tech blades.

gear.name: Ammo, 5 Rounds
gear.description: For simplicity's sake, ammo is considered fungible between guns without concern for caliber. Sold in bundles of five rounds; reload a weapon's magazine from a stock of this ammo.

gear.name: Ammo, Empty Magazine
gear.description: An empty magazine. Individual magazines need to be kept loaded with loose ammo if quick reloads are desired.

gear.name: Backpack
gear.description: Strength alone won't help a survivor carry their gear if they've got nothing to carry it in. No Encumbrance while worn.

gear.name: Batteries, Modern-Day
gear.description: Non-rechargeable modern batteries in whatever format the PCs may need.

gear.name: Binoculars
gear.description: If something is close enough for a survivor to notice it, most binoculars will let them get a good look.

gear.name: Camping Kit
gear.description: Cooking gear, stakes, a tinderbox, cordage, and other small necessities. Without this kit or intense primitive-tech experience, a survivor may not be able to make a fire or cook a meal at all.

gear.name: Clothes, Basic
gear.description: Ordinary long-lasting clothing. No Encumbrance while worn.

gear.name: Clothes, Cold Weather
gear.description: Insulated clothing for extreme climates. Without the right gear, survivors might suffer privation in the cold. No Encumbrance while worn.

gear.name: Compressed Fuel for One Night
gear.description: Compressed charcoal or other high-density fuel, useful when firewood can't be gathered or foraged.

gear.name: Crowbar
gear.description: Breaking bars, demo axes, and similar prying tools for getting through rubble; can also serve as a makeshift club.

gear.name: Dog, Trained
gear.description: A trained fighting dog. A single PC can't manage more fighting dogs at once than the sum of their Charisma modifier and Lead skill, or Work if it's animal-handling experience.

gear.name: Drone, with Controller
gear.description: A simple civilian-grade flying observation drone, range 5 kilometers and 30-minute run time on a modern battery. Easily spotted by wary observers, AC 20 in flight, and downed by any damage. A tech with Fix-1 can rig it to carry a grenade, halving its flight time.

gear.name: Energy Cell, Type A
gear.description: A small cylinder that powers personal-scale TL4 gear and can substitute for modern batteries in simple gear. Non-rechargeable.

gear.name: Energy Cell, Type A+
gear.description: A rechargeable variant of the Type A cell, rechargeable with a day of conventional mains power but more fragile. Not commonly found for sale; usually looted from an intact cache.

gear.name: Energy Cell, Type B
gear.description: A large, heavy cell that fuels vehicles and heavy equipment. Non-rechargeable.

gear.name: Energy Cell, Type B+
gear.description: A rechargeable variant of the Type B cell, rechargeable with a week of conventional mains power but more fragile. Not commonly found for sale; usually looted from an intact cache.

gear.name: First Aid Kit
gear.description: Bandages, antibiotics, splints, and other tools of immediate lifesaving importance. A medic without such a kit suffers significant penalties treating injuries or disease. After each use, roll 1d6; on a 1, the kit has run out of useful materials.

gear.name: Flashlight
gear.description: A modern battery powers this handheld light for 6 hours, casting an effective beam 20 meters long and 3 meters wide.

gear.name: Gas Mask
gear.description: Filters out airborne toxins and inhaled gases, but applies a -2 penalty to hit rolls and Notice checks due to restricted vision.

gear.name: Hand Cart
gear.description: Carries either 15 units of Encumbrance or one helpless rider without significantly slowing overland travel, given fresh hands to trade off pulling it. Can't readily cross rough terrain.

gear.name: Hand Tool
gear.description: Saws, wood axes, adzes, hammers, and other tools in high demand when civilization needs rebuilding.

gear.name: Horse, Riding
gear.description: A riding horse, not trained for combat and prone to panic in a fight. Combat-trained steeds cost twice as much where they can be had; actual warhorses are eight times as much in the few societies that can raise them.

gear.name: Lantern
gear.description: A hooded oil lantern casting light in a 10-meter radius, burning 4 hours on one flask of oil, protected from rain or wind.

gear.name: Lockpick Kit
gear.description: Carefully-bent wire picks, skeleton keys, and keycard spoofers, allowing lockpick attempts on mechanical and electronic locks.

gear.name: Mule
gear.description: Steady, stubborn, and slow, a mule can carry 15 items of Encumbrance while grazing for most of its needed food. Not useful in combat, but rarely spooked and small enough for human-sized corridors.

gear.name: Night Vision Gear
gear.description: Somewhat bulky, applying a -1 penalty to Notice checks, but allows normal vision in dark environments for three hours per modern battery loaded into it.

gear.name: Oil Flask
gear.description: Oil or kerosene, usable to fuel a lantern or spilled to create a 1-meter pool of flame doing 1d6 damage to creatures caught in it (Evasion negates). The pool lasts 1d6 rounds.

gear.name: Radio, Long-Distance
gear.description: A long-range ham rig requiring an appropriate background or Program-0 skill to operate effectively, but able to reach hundreds of kilometers given a few hours to make the connection. Functions about a week on one set of modern batteries.

gear.name: Radio, Walkie-Talkie
gear.description: A simple handheld radio with a reliable range of 1 kilometer in the open or 200 meters in a city. Functions about a week on one set of modern batteries.

gear.name: Rope, 20m
gear.description: Twenty meters of light, strong nylon rope with a hundred uses.

gear.name: Scrap, TL2
gear.description: Salvaged debris of TL2 sophistication, used to build or repair gear of the same tech level.

gear.name: Scrap, TL3
gear.description: Salvaged debris of TL3 sophistication, used to build or repair gear of the same tech level.

gear.name: Sleeping Bag
gear.description: A bedroll, long cloak, or sleeping bag, needed for adequate sleep outside of warm climates.

gear.name: Surgical Kit
gear.description: A heavy case of tools and drugs, no substitute for an actual medical facility but enough for complicated surgery to be minimally feasible. No risk of running out if used only for a small PC party's needs.

gear.name: Tarp
gear.description: A waterproof tarp roughly 3 meters square, serving as a makeshift tent or shelter cover.

gear.name: Tent
gear.description: A proper tent for two friendly survivors, sufficient to keep the rain and wind off.

gear.name: Torches, 3
gear.description: Simple wooden sticks with pitch-and-cloth heads or similar slow-burning substances. Each torch burns for an hour, casting light in a 10-meter radius.

gear.name: Toolkit
gear.description: A portable toolkit with the implements needed to fix most TL2 or TL3 equipment, or manufacture TL0 or TL1 gear from scrap.

gear.name: Water Jug
gear.description: A plastic or metal container holding enough water to sustain a person for one day in temperate climates.

gear.name: Alcohol, Common
gear.description: A dose is enough to render a drinker pleasantly tipsy. Effects last 1d4 hours: -1 Stress gained during that time, but -2 to hit rolls and -1 to skill checks.

gear.name: Alcohol, Excellent
gear.description: A finer vintage with the same mechanical effects as common alcohol: 1d4 hours, -1 Stress gained during that time, but -2 to hit rolls and -1 to skill checks.

gear.name: Antibiotics, Common
gear.description: Treats Mild or Severe diseases, allowing a reroll of a failed disease save. Multiple doses allow multiple rerolls, up to the attending physician's Heal skill (minimum once).

gear.name: Antibiotics, Powerful
gear.description: Treats even Lethal diseases, allowing a reroll of a failed disease save. Multiple doses allow multiple rerolls, up to the attending physician's Heal skill (minimum once). Requires Heal-0 to apply.

gear.name: Depressant, Crude
gear.description: Removes one point of Stress, once per day.

gear.name: Depressant, Refined
gear.description: Removes 2 points of Stress and ends any current Breakdown, but adds 1 System Strain. Requires Heal-0 to apply.

gear.name: Hallucinogen, Crude
gear.description: Incapacitates the user for 1 hour, but ends any current Breakdown.

gear.name: Hallucinogen, Refined
gear.description: Ends any current Breakdown, lasting 1d4 hours, removing 1d4 Stress but adding 1 System Strain. Requires Heal-0 to apply.

gear.name: Opioid, Crude
gear.description: Grants 1d10 temporary hit points for an hour, which can exceed the user's normal maximum. The points vanish at the hour's end, leaving at least 1 HP. Adds 1 System Strain the first time the user takes damage while affected.

gear.name: Opioid, Refined
gear.description: Rolls 1d10 twice and takes the higher result for temporary hit points, otherwise as crude opioids. Requires Heal-0 to apply.

gear.name: Stimulant, Crude
gear.description: Lasts one hour; once during that time, as an Instant action, add +2 to a hit roll or +1 to a skill check, gaining 1 System Strain if used.

gear.name: Stimulant, Refined
gear.description: As crude stimulants, but the effect lasts 24 hours and makes sleep unnecessary and impossible during that time. Requires Heal-0 to apply.

gear.name: Therapeutic, Common
gear.description: Applied to a person who suffered a Major Injury within the past scene, allows a reroll of any failed saving throw that injury forced, with a bonus equal to the physician's Heal skill. Only one reroll. Requires Heal-0 to apply.

gear.name: Therapeutic, Powerful
gear.description: As common therapeutics, but can be applied up to a week after the injury if the victim has survived that long. Requires Heal-1 to apply.

gear.name: Bounce
gear.description: A nano-fueled invisible force shield bubbles the user, protecting them completely from the next kinetic injury they would otherwise suffer in the next hour. Adds 2 System Strain.

gear.name: Glow
gear.description: Cures up to 1d6 points of Constitution lost to radiation damage. Requires Heal-1 to apply.

gear.name: Lifestyle
gear.description: A cosmetic and hygienic tab whose therapeutic substrate heals 1d6+1 lost hit points. The user gains 1 System Strain if it heals them.

gear.name: Morning After
gear.description: Negates any non-lethal toxin in the user, at the cost of 1 System Strain.

gear.name: Panacea
gear.description: Immediately cures any non-biowarfare disease, though there is a 1 in 6 chance it worsens the disease by one degree instead, or instantly kills the victim of a Lethal disease. Requires Heal-2 to apply.

gear.name: Smile
gear.description: A social disinhibitor lasting 1d6 hours, increasing the user's Charisma modifier by +1 (up to +2 maximum) for 1 point of System Strain. A natural 12 on a social skill check while affected is an automatic failure.

gear.name: Snooze
gear.description: An over-the-counter sleep aid granting 8 hours of restful sleep regardless of discomfort, hunger, or privation, for full normal recovery. The user falls asleep 1d6 rounds after taking it and cannot be awoken early.

gear.name: Thunderbolt
gear.description: Lasts one scene. As an On Turn action once per round, the user takes a bonus Main Action. Each use adds 1d4 System Strain, one cumulative die per trigger in the scene; if this pushes System Strain over the user's maximum, their heart explodes once the action completes. Requires Heal-1 to apply.

gear.name: Titan
gear.description: A Harmony Bureau enforcer's performance drug lasting one hour: +2 to hit rolls, +1 to Strength and Dexterity modifiers (up to +2 maximum), and 6 extra temporary hit points lost before any others. Adds 1 System Strain. Requires Heal-0 to apply.

gear.name: Trauma Patch
gear.description: Stabilizes a Mortally Wounded victim on a successful Int or Dex/Heal check against difficulty 6 plus 1 per full round since they went down. A failed attempt can be retried with a fresh patch; useless after six rounds. Cannot revive victims downed by poison, explosives, or other massive trauma. Unlike most stims, this is bulky and counts as one item of Encumbrance.

gear.name: Weeper
gear.description: An emergency purge tab causing the victim to weep, vomit, and sweat out any poisons in their body, and grants an immediate Physical save to cure any Mild or Severe disease. The user gains 2 System Strain and is incapacitated for 1d6 rounds while it takes effect.

gear.name: Zen
gear.description: Temporarily suppresses any Breakdown or psychic scar for 24 hours, making it impossible to gain Stress during that time. The enforced calm compels a successful Mental save before any violent action, the action wasted on failure.
